q: Relative density is how much a substance is denser than ____.
e: Relative density is how much a substance is denser than water. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Relative density is also known as ____.
e: Relative density is also known as specific gravity. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: As the density of water is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units, then density of substance can be taken as the ____.
e: As the density of water is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units, then density of substance can be taken as the relative density. Relative density here means mass per unit volume. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: As the relative density is the ratio of two densities, it is just a number without ____.
e: As the relative density is the ratio of two densities, it is just a number without unit. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: When an object is partially (or) totally immersed in a liquid, the object displaces liquid volume that is equal to the volume of the ____ portion.
e: When an object is partially (or) totally immersed in a liquid, the object displaces liquid volume that is equal to the volume of the immersed portion. The physics in this sentence is built around immersed.

q: The loss in weight of the object is equal to the weight of the ____ displaced.
e: The loss in weight of the object is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: The upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed partially or totally in a liquid is equal to the ____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: The upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed partially or totally in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by the body. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: upward thrust = uplift force = ____ = weight of liquid displaced
e: Upward thrust = uplift force = buoyancy = weight of liquid displaced. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: By Archimedes' principle, weight of a body is more than buoyancy (or) upward thrust, it will ____ in the liquid.
e: By Archimedes' principle, weight of a body is more than buoyancy (or) upward thrust, it will sink in the liquid. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Substances having relative density greater than ____ will sink in water.
e: Substances having relative density greater than one will sink in water. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: King of ____ was suspicious with his crown; King let Archimedes to test whether the crown was made of pure gold.
e: King of Syracuse was suspicious with his crown; King let Archimedes to test whether the crown was made of pure gold. The physics in this sentence is built around Syracuse.

q: The crown had mass 3.75 kg or ____ g.
e: The crown had mass 3.75 kg or 3750 g. The physics in this sentence is built around 3750.

q: As the density of gold is $19.3 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, the crown must have volume ____ $\text{cm}^3$.
e: As the density of gold is $19.3 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, the crown must have volume 194 $\text{cm}^3$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Archimedes found that the volume (by his principle Part I) was ____ $\text{cm}^3$.
e: Archimedes found that the volume (by his principle Part I) was 315 $\text{cm}^3$. The physics in this sentence is built around 315.

q: Then, he answered to the King that the crown was not ____.
e: Then, he answered to the King that the crown was not pure gold. The physics in this sentence is built around pure gold.

q: The added metal is ____ because it has similar color.
e: The added metal is copper because it has similar color. The physics in this sentence is built around copper.

q: The student can extend the problem why the gold smith did not use ____ metal instead of copper.
e: The student can extend the problem why the gold smith did not use lead metal instead of copper. The physics in this sentence is built around lead.

q: The relative density of sulphur is ____.
